fig1_val_curves.png.caption: GSM8K validation accuracy vs training step: the identical signed_ema merger holds near the dense ceiling at anchor latency K=5 (stops measured at step 50, pre-spiral) but collapses below the no-merger floor at K=20, falling from 0.648 at step 50 to 0.444 by step 100 as the length spiral ignites around step 93.
fig1_val_curves.png.alt_text: Line chart of validation accuracy versus step showing dense (~0.766, flat) and K=5 (~0.736) staying high while the K=20 curve rises then collapses from 0.648 to 0.444 below the 0.6300 no-merger floor.

fig2_collapse_mechanism.png.caption: Mechanism of the K=20 collapse (EXP-37, steps 1-100): the response-length mean ratchets from ~251 to 683 tokens in the final ignition window (steps ~91-100); policy entropy falls across the run from 5.78 (step 1) to 0.42 (step 100), the bulk at merger onset (~step 11), and during the spiral (steps ~92-100) it continues ~0.7->0.42 as a follower rather than the trigger; PG clip fraction spikes at every Q-refresh (cadence fingerprint; see section 5), with a ~0.004-0.06 floor between refreshes once the merger engages (after the ~10-step warmup), rising toward the back half.
fig2_collapse_mechanism.png.alt_text: Three stacked time-series panels for the K=20 run: response length climbing sharply at the end, entropy steadily falling, and clip fraction showing periodic spikes at every Q-refresh step.

fig3_staleness_schematic.png.caption: Schematic mechanism (illustrative, axes not measured): staleness error norm grows with anchor latency K as the sum of a linear weight-drift term and a super-linear off-policy distribution-shift term, so K=5 sits in the sub-critical stable region while K=20 crosses the ignition threshold into the super-critical regime.
fig3_staleness_schematic.png.alt_text: Conceptual plot of staleness error versus latency K showing a linear drift curve, a super-linear off-policy curve, and their steep total, with a stable green band at K=5 and a red ignition band at K=20 above a dashed threshold line.
